paths.description: Homepage catalog and age/consent entry state; represents the primary listing template and initial journey.
Tags index; represents the extremely long taxonomy/listing archetype.
Representative video detail; covers player metadata, media behavior, related content, structured data, and share metadata.
Search with no results; represents the primary form and empty-state recovery.
Privacy policy; covers trust, disclosure, and long-form content structure.
Representative HTTP failure route; covers recovery behavior.
Login, payment, subscription, and account flows were not covered because robots excludes these routes and valid user credentials/commitments were not supplied.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode probe matched prefers-color-scheme: dark but computed html color-scheme remained normal and body remained rgb(214,214,214); the dark screenshot retained the same fixed palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark support in an early color-scheme meta tag and on :root, then express surface and text tokens with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme rule.

findings.summary: Long listing pages provide no responsive scroll-state navigation cues.
findings.evidence: The 9,371px homepage and 22,651px mobile document had no visible sticky navigation or progress state; the fixed-element probe found only consent/ad overlays.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep primary navigation available without covering content and add a lightweight scroll-state cue or return affordance on very long indexes.

findings.summary: Navigation changes do not visibly preserve or cue location.
findings.evidence: Representative routes reload as conventional documents, while the inspected CSS and screenshots exposed no current-section marker, transition cue, or post-navigation highlight.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the current section with aria-current and a clear visual state; use directional transitions only where they clarify route hierarchy and respect reduced motion.

findings.summary: Consent and age-gate overlays are custom div structures rather than semantic dialogs.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found .age-popup, .cookiesBanner, and #agego-overlay-container fixed divs, with no dialog or role=dialog element.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a modal dialog with an accessible name, focus containment, Escape/cancel behavior where legally allowed, and restore focus after dismissal. Use a non-modal semantic banner for cookies.

findings.summary: Advertising and promotional chrome competes heavily with the core catalog.
findings.evidence: The first 100 links included four prominent outbound promotions, the HAR recorded 118 third-party requests, and the video route reported many advertising/autoplay media elements around the core player.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve a clearly labelled, bounded ad region; remove duplicate ad providers and autoplay creatives; keep the catalog and player as the dominant visual hierarchy.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only and does not adapt reusable components to their containers.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules or container-type declarations even though cards and ad placements are reused in different-width grids.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card and ad-shell components containment and use size container queries for typography, metadata, and action layout.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not consistently visible.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reported outline none on the age-entry button and outline 0 on the visible cookie OK button; Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.69.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible treatment with sufficient contrast to every interactive control and verify the complete tab sequence at mobile and desktop sizes.

findings.summary: Failure and empty states do not offer useful recovery.
findings.evidence: An empty search says only “There is no data in this list,” and the representative missing route returns a bare “Not Found” page without search, navigation, or a route home.
findings.suggestedFix: Add suggested queries and a clear route back from empty search, and serve a branded 404 with navigation, search, and a concise recovery message.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is well outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.9s, FCP 2.9s, Speed Index 5.6s, and TTI 8.9s; the independent trace measured LCP 5.70s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP resource, eliminate parser-blocking scripts ahead of content, and delay ad/analytics work until after the main catalog is rendered.

findings.summary: The page performs excessive main-thread work and occasionally produces a severe long task.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 2.4s of main-thread work and 110ms TBT; the mobile layout observer captured a 1,552ms long task around 3.45s.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the ad and legacy script work, remove unnecessary providers, split long work, and schedule non-critical tasks after content and user input.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and weak caching delay delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR and DOM confirmation identified lang_redirect.js and verify.js in head without async/defer, plus multiple synchronous body scripts; Lighthouse estimated 640ms render-blocking and 925KiB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only essential gate state, defer non-critical scripts, replace document-order dependencies with modules, and apply long-lived immutable caching to versioned assets.

findings.summary: Large unused, legacy, and duplicated script payloads ship on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 874KiB unused JavaScript and 53KiB legacy JavaScript; the DOM includes four sequential main.min bundles and many repeated ad-provider scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate the four main bundles, remove dead and legacy branches, and load each ad integration once only when its placement becomes eligible.

findings.summary: Controls, images, frames, and landmarks have incomplete accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt, frame-title, link-name, and accessibility-tree audits; the image primitive found six missing alt attributes and the DOM exposed no main/nav/header/footer landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide names for every actionable link/control, titles for frames, meaningful or empty alt text as appropriate, and semantic main/nav/header/footer landmarks.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed, and the forced-colors screenshot shows visual elements relying on hard-coded colors rather than an explicitly supported contrast scheme.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct failing token pairs to WCAG contrast minimums and test controls in forced-colors and prefers-contrast modes without suppressing system colors.

findings.summary: Landmark structure and focus indication are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The page has no main, nav, header, or footer landmarks in the probe, and visible controls such as cookie OK have no focus outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce a logical landmark and heading hierarchy, add a skip link, and ensure each focus stop has an obvious focus-visible style.

findings.summary: Zoom is constrained and video alternatives are absent.
findings.evidence: The viewport sets maximum-scale=1.0, which Lighthouse flags because it prevents robust zoom beyond 100%; the sampled detail page had no text tracks and multiple autoplay videos.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale, preserve reflow at 200 to 400 percent zoom, provide captions or transcripts for meaningful media, and avoid autoplay for non-essential video.

findings.summary: Several ad images render at incorrect aspect ratios.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio and identified 100x250 rendering for 300x250 creatives; its unsized-images audit also only partially passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use numeric width and height attributes matching intrinsic ratios, then constrain responsively with width:100% and height:auto.

findings.summary: Deprecated synchronous network behavior and browser inspector issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a synchronous XMLHttpRequest deprecation and failed the Chrome inspector-issues audit for cookie-related problems.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace synchronous XHR with asynchronous fetch, update the calling integration, and clear all DevTools Issues panel findings in a clean profile.

findings.summary: No usable sitemap was exposed at the conventional sitemap URL.
findings.evidence: robots.txt was available and allowed public pages, but /sitemap.xml returned no sitemap content during recon.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a current XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt; keep canonical and hreflang URLs consistent with sitemap entries.

findings.summary: Homepage share/entity metadata is incomplete and detail metadata is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found JSON-LD but no Open Graph tags; on the video page og:url uses a different /video/767143/ URL shape from the canonical URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and Open Graph metadata on indexes, and make og:url exactly match the canonical detail URL.

findings.summary: Core transport defenses and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, or X-Content-Type-Options; all four cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None, including three 400-day cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and nosniff, introduce a nonce/hash CSP in report-only then enforcement mode, and set Secure plus the narrowest viable SameSite value and lifetime on every cookie.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising begin before meaningful consent and dominate network activity.
findings.evidence: The tracker scan found 16 third-party origins, Google Analytics, and 64 requests to s.pemsrv.com; the HAR attributed 118 of 125 requests and 1.37MB to third parties while only a passive cookie banner was shown.
findings.suggestedFix: Default non-essential analytics and ads off until valid consent, reduce vendors, document each purpose and retention period, and offer equally prominent accept/reject controls.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced privacy and isolation policies are mostly absent.
findings.evidence: Only X-Frame-Options was present; Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/frame-ancestors, and HSTS were absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, express frame-ancestors in CSP, retain clickjacking defense, and assess Trusted Types for ad-rich script surfaces.

findings.summary: HTTP failure recovery degrades to a server-default dead end.
findings.evidence: The sampled nonexistent route displayed only “Not Found” with no site navigation, retry, search, or home link.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded, lightweight 404 with the normal navigation, search, and clear recovery links while retaining a correct 404 status.

findings.summary: Advertising is mixed into content and tracking starts before a meaningful choice.
findings.evidence: Recon found locally targeted promotional cards pointing back to the homepage among catalog links, while analytics/ad requests fired before the cookie banner offered only an OK action.
findings.suggestedFix: Label every paid placement unambiguously, separate it visually from catalog cards, and replace one-sided consent with clear accept, reject, and settings choices before tracking.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not responsive or consistently modern.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 94 lacked srcset, 15 used legacy formats, and nine were more than twice their displayed width; Lighthouse estimated further image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and width-based srcsets, size candidates to card containers, and reserve high priority only for the actual LCP image.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics generate disproportionate work and requests.
findings.evidence: The load made 125 requests, including 68 fetch/XHR requests and 64 requests to one ad origin; mobile observation captured a 1.55s long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop background refresh when hidden, batch telemetry, cap ad calls per view, and schedule non-critical processing during idle periods only.

findings.summary: Third-party and autoplay media costs are not proportionate to the first-view task.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse transferred 9,145KiB in its run; representative pages exposed many autoplay ad videos, and 118 of 125 HAR requests were third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, lazy-load one clearly labelled placement at a time, disable autoplay creatives, and unload media outside the viewport.

taskList.title: Block non-essential tracking until consent and reduce advertising vendors
Deploy CSP, HSTS, secure cookie attributes, and browser policies
Remove render-blocking and duplicated JavaScript to recover LCP
Repair accessible semantics, contrast, focus, zoom, and media alternatives
Optimize responsive image delivery and impose media budgets
Use semantic consent/age dialogs and reduce surrounding chrome
Add useful empty, 404, and navigation recovery states
Correct document assets and browser hygiene
Add user-driven dark mode and component-level responsiveness
